summary: Mozambique waives visas for SADC citizens and, since a 2023 decree, for about 30 major tourism-source countries including the US, UK and much of Western Europe (30 days, with a small border-processing fee), while other nationalities can obtain a simplified tourist visa at the border or apply online.

payments.text: Cards are accepted in Maputo hotels, supermarkets and the bigger beach lodges; everywhere else cash rules. US dollars and South African rand are widely taken in tourist areas, but carry small metical notes up-country.

safety.text: The southern and central tourist areas — Maputo, Inhambane, Tofo, Vilankulo and the Bazaruto archipelago — are generally calm, though petty crime and police document checks are common. Avoid Cabo Delgado province in the far north, where an armed insurgency continues.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Mozambique Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to October is the dry, cooler season — ideal for beaches, diving and safaris. November to April is hot and humid, with cyclone risk along the coast roughly January to March.

tips.text: Avoid Cabo Delgado province in the far north, where an insurgency continues, including Pemba's surroundings when advisories say so. The main beach destinations from Maputo up to Vilankulo are far from the affected area.
Carry your passport with entry stamp (or a notarised copy) at all times — police checkpoints are frequent and fines for missing documents are common.
If you need a border visa, bring the fee in US dollar cash — card terminals at land borders are unreliable. Rand are usually accepted at crossings from South Africa and Eswatini.
Cyclone and heavy-rain season runs roughly December to March, especially along the central and northern coast — roads flood and ferries stop. Check forecasts if traveling in that window.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Mozambique?
faq.answer: Many tourists no longer do. SADC citizens enter free, and under a 2023 decree citizens of about 30 major tourism-source countries — including the US, UK, Portugal and most of Western Europe — enter visa-free for up to 30 days, paying only a small border-processing fee. Everyone else can get a simplified tourist visa at the border or apply online at evisa.gov.mz.

faq.question: What is the border fee for visa-free visitors?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt tourists under the 2023 scheme pay a processing fee of about MZN 650 (roughly USD 10) on arrival. Bring cash — meticais, dollars or rand are normally accepted.

faq.question: Can I get a Mozambique visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Yes — the simplified border-visa regime lets tourists from most remaining countries obtain a 30-day visa at airports and major land borders for roughly USD 50 in cash. Applying in advance through evisa.gov.mz is safer if you want to avoid lines or arrive at a small crossing.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Mozambique?
faq.answer: Yes — tourist stays can normally be extended once, for up to 30 further days, at migration service (migração) offices in provincial capitals. Apply before your current permission expires; overstays are fined per day.

faq.question: Is Mozambique safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The main beach circuit in the south and center is generally fine with normal precautions. The serious security problem is confined to Cabo Delgado province in the far north. Check current advisories, carry your documents, and avoid driving at night.
